Today we will talk about the top 10 places for a two-day

Our list is headed by one of the most popular
directions from Bangalore, Pondicherry, officially known
as Puducherry.
Pondicherry is an ideal place for a two-day trip from
Bangalore.
Pondicherry can offer much more than you think.
The streets of the French Quarter, also known as the White
City, are decorated with charming mustard yellow
facades and bougainvillea flowers.
This is an ideal place for creativity and stunning
photos.
Walking through the French Quarter, you will see dozens
of cozy cafes and restaurants where they serve
delightful French cuisine.
If you are attracted to spirituality, go to Matrimandir
in Auroville.
More details about Auroville and other places I told
in my video about the sights of Pondicherry.
I will leave a link to this video in the description below.
There are wonderful beaches in Pondicherry.
If you want a quiet rest away from the city
bustle, go to the Serenity beach.
If you want to enjoy an evening walk along the
shore, go to the Promenade beach, also known as the
rocky beach.
If you want to swim, go to the Paradise beach.
If you live in Bangalore, the best way to get to
Pondicherry is by train.
The schedule of trains is perfect for a weekend
trip from Bangalore.
The second on the list is Kurg, which is called
Scotland and India.
Kurg is located in the western ghats of the Sahyidri mountains,
only 250 km from Bangalore.
From waterfalls to mountains, from adventure trekking
to temples, from coffee plantations to Kodavu cuisine,
Kurg has everything you can wish for.
The weather in Kurg is pleasant all year round, although,
according to the recommendations, the best time to visit
Kurg is winter and summer.
You can visit Kurg and in the season of musons.
At this time, there are heavy rains, but if you, like
us, love rain, do not hesitate to miss the
subsoil of Kurg in the season of musons.
In Kurg, there are an infinite number of places to inspect
Mandalapatti, Talakaviri, Abbi waterfall, Chikliholy
reservoir, Golden Temple, Slanovi Lager-Dubari, Tadyandamol,
Waterfalls and Rupa, Malvalli, Platina-Kharangi.
Oh, this list can be continued endlessly.
All these places are so beautiful that you may want
to extend your two-day trip to three days.
More detailed information about these places you can
find in my video Top 10 places to visit in Kurg.
We all know that the plans to go to Goa are always
broken down, so instead of Goa, it is better to plan a trip
to Gokarna, it is called Little Goa, but it is even
more beautiful.
Many of the Taiga always moved to untouched
beaches of Gokarna, where there are fewer crowds, and the beaches themselves are much cleaner.
Over the past decade, a huge stream of tourists has
In fact, this trend has divided Gokarna into two parts.
One, for pilgrims who come to ask for blessings
from Shiva, the other, for carefree travelers looking
for peace in the embrace of nature.
Gokarna beaches are one of the most beautiful and clean in India.
Such places as the beaches of Half Moon and Paradise are so
isolated that you can only get to them on foot
or on a boat.
I advise you to arrange a beach tour and visit everything in turn
Gokarna beach, Om, Kudle, Paradise and Half Moon.
Here you can do water sports or, if you want
lazy rest, just relax in one of the beach
cafes.
Enjoy the sunset with your favorite beer in your hand.
Gokarna is not only beaches.
For believers, the Mahabaleshwar temple is of great importance.
The temple is dedicated to the Lord Shiva, and one of the most powerful
of the Malingams is stored in it.

The next in the list is Uda Gamandalam, better known as Uti.
Located in the western ghats, Uti took in high mountains,
incredible lakes, dense forests, endless meadows
and endless tea plantations.
This mountain resort is the edge of mesmerizing places,
it is not in vain that it is called the queen of mountain stations.
Uti is so popular among tourists that it may seem
too commercial, but let it not prevent you from visiting it,
because there are stunning views and climate.
Just choose time for a trip when there are no tourists.
I highly recommend visiting Kunur, where there are
comparatively fewer people and even more beautiful.
You can take a walk on the tea plantations, find out how they make tea,
or just leisurely ride a boat across the lake Uti.
In short, Uti will never disappoint you with its beauty.
If you are not a tea lover, let me invite you to the country of coffee, Chikmagalur.
It is believed that it was in Baba Budangiri in Chikmagalur
that in 1670, for the first time, coffee was grown in the country.
All thanks to Baba Budan, who brought seven un-fried coffee
herbs to Chikmagalur, returning from Hajj.
I have been to Chikmagalur many times, and every time he surprised me.

The local landscapes are so beautiful that they resemble

You can climb the highest peak of Karnataka, Mulla and Nagiri,

The list of places you can visit in Chikmagalur is endless.

Next on our list is Wayanat.
Wayanat is famous for its touristic paths, fascinating waterfalls, caves,
places to watch birds and stunning views.
I like the local green rice fields and high coconut palms.
A walk along the endless rice fields is a great pleasure.
You can visit many places, such as Kurova Island,
cave Idakkal, Sintinel Rock waterfall, Banasura-Sagar plateau,
Nelimala observation deck and Pichimbra peak.
In addition to typical tourist places, you can get acquainted with tribes
that still live on the forest, mining food and everything necessary.
Wayanat has many great resorts,
which also offer active rest.
Next on the list is the favorite place for tourists, Sokleshpur.
Sokleshpur is a small town located at the foot of the Western Ghats.
There are charming views that are breathtaking.
There are many resorts in Sokleshpur, where you will feel closer to nature.
These resorts are the perfect place for those who are looking for adventures
or just want to spend time with friends and family.
In addition to Fort Manjarabad, there are no such observation decks in Sokleshpur
or Chikmagaluri.
But there are other activities that will not let you get bored.
You can go on a short hike along the nearby hills,
take active rest at the resort, watch beautiful birds
or just relax in the pool.
On your way back to Bangalore, you can also visit
Belur, Halebidu and the Church of Shittihalli.
If you live in Bangalore, then you have probably seen restaurants
at the edge of almost every corner of the city.
If you want to know the origins of the real South Indian cuisine,
you should visit Udupi.
Udupi is an coastal district in Karnataka,
famous for the Shri Krishna temple, beaches,
educational and financial institutions, as well as delicious food.
Lately, Udupi has become a popular tourist destination.
There is something to do in Udupi.
You can visit the Shri Krishna temple, where you can see the deity through the window,
take care of the kayaking in Mulki,
visit the most beautiful island of St. Mary or visit the cleanest beach in India,
Padubidri.
The list of places is endless.

Be sure to watch it.
Mysore is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the state of Karnataka.
Thanks to the rich cultural heritage and amazing royal history,
Mysore was the main city of Karnataka even before Bangalore.
Mysore is one of the cleanest cities in India.
Although modernity affects other cities,
Mysore managed to preserve its heritage,
which made tourism one of the most prosperous industries in the city.
The city carefully keeps traditions, magnificent palaces,
beautiful gardens and magnificent temples.
Mysore Palace is one of the most visited palaces in India.
In addition to the palace, you can also visit the hills of Chamundi,
the Cathedral of St. Philomene, the gardens of Brindavan and the Mysore Zoo.
I guarantee that the time spent in Mysore will be unforgettable for you.
Iyerkot, which is often called a duck for the poor,
is one of the most budgetary mountain resorts in India.
Iyerkot is located in the state of Tamil Nadu,
just 200 km from Bangalore.
Its name Iyerkot came from Lake Iyerkot and its surrounding forest.
In Tamil language, Eri means lake, and Kadu means forest.
Thus, these two words together form Iyerkot, which means lake forest.
This is a great option for a weekend trip from Bangalore.
There are many attractions in Iyerkot, from lakes and sightseeing sites to gardens and waterfalls.
You can visit Lake Iyerkot, deer park, botanical garden,
Kiliyur waterfall, ladies' seat and Pagadupoin.
